In this case interaction energy is inversely proportional to the sixth power of the distance between two interacting particles.

Ammonia is a polar molecule it has a net dipole moment and hydrogen is a non-polar molecule as its net dipole moment is zero.In this pair of molecule dipole-induced dipole interactions exist.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct order of decreasing acidic nature of oxides
questions.solution:
A binary compound of oxygen with another element is called oxide

Oxides can be simple (e.g., MgO, Al2O3 ) or mixed (Pb3O4 ,Fe3O4 ). Simple oxides can be classified on the basis of their acidic, basic or amphoteric character. An oxide that combines with water to give an acid is termed acidic oxide (e.g., SO2 ,Cl2O7,CO2 , N2O5 ). For example, SO2 combines with water to give H2SO3 , an acid.

 The oxides which give a base with water are known as basic oxides (e.g., Na2O, CaO, BaO). For example, CaO combines with water to give Ca(OH)2, a base.

Some metallic oxides exhibit a dual behaviour. They show characteristics of both acidic as well as basic oxides. Such oxides are known as amphoteric oxides. They react with acids as well as alkalies. For example, Al2O3 reacts with acids as well as alkalies.

There are some oxides which are neither acidic nor basic. Such oxides are known as neutral oxides. Examples of neutral oxides are CO, NO and N2O.

Period 2 Li Be B C N

According to periodic trend, the electronegativity of the period 2 elements increases in the order :

Li < Be < B < C < N

Electronegativty of the  central atom of the oxide is direclty proportional acidic nature of the oxide.

Therefore, the acidic character of their oxides decreases in the order as follows :

questions.solution: The given solution of methyl alcohol and acetic acid is a non-ideal solution. When a solution does not obey Raoult’s law over the entire range of concentration, then it is called non-ideal solution. The vapour pressure of such a solution is either higher or lower than that predicted by Raoult’s law. If it is higher, the solution exhibits positive deviation and if it is lower, it exhibits negative deviation from Raoult’s law. In case of negative deviations from Raoult’s law, the intermolecular attractive forces between A-A and B-B are weaker than those between A-B and leads to decrease in vapour pressure resulting in negative deviations. Statement II is true, but Statement I is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution:
Given,

ℝ be the set of all real numbers.

Now solving statement I : The function f:-π2,π2→ℝ defined by fx=secx+tanx

Now differentiating the function with respect to x we get,

f'x=secxsecx+tanx

Now we know that secx is always positive in given domain and secx+tanx will also be positive as tanx is negative in -π2,0 but secx≥tanx in -π2,0

So, f'x≥0 hence it is a one - one function.

Now solving statement II : The function f:[0,∞)→ℝ defined by

fx=x2

Differentiating the function we get,

f'x=2x

⇒f'x≥0 ∀ x∈[0,∞)

Hence it is also a one-one function.

So both are true.

questions.solution:
Given,

A, B & C are independent so,

PA∩B=PAPB

PB∩B=PBPC

PC∩A=PCPA

And given PB¯∪C¯=12

Now,

PB¯∩C¯A=PB¯∩C¯∩APA

By diagram we can see,

PB¯∩C¯∩A=PA−PA∩B−PA∩C+PA∩B∩C

Also, PB¯∪C¯=12

⇒1−PB∩C=12

⇒PBPC=12

Rewriting,

PB¯∩C¯∩A=PA−PAPB−PAPC+PAPBPC

⇒PB¯∩C¯∩A=PA1−PB−PC+12

⇒PB¯∩C¯∩APA=1−PB−PC+12

⇒PB¯∩C¯∩APA=32−b−C

So, PB¯∩C¯A=32−b−C

questions.solution:
Given,

Two dices are thrown so total sample space will be 36,

Now let the sum of numbers appearing on dice be a multiple of 4 be event A,

So outcomes of event A will be 2,2,1,3,3,1,5,3,3,5,6,2,2,6,4,4,6,6→9

So probability will be PA=936=14

Now let the event 4 has already occured be B,

So outcomes will be 1,4,4,1,2,4,4,2,3,4,4,3,4,4,4,5,5,4,4,6,6,4→11

So probability will be PB=1136

So PA∩B=136

Now PB|A=PA∩BPA=136936=19

So, 3p+2=3×19+2=73

questions.q: A river has a steady speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math>. A man swims upstream at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> and swims back to the starting point in total time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math>. The man can swim at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>v</mi></math> in still water. If the time taken by the man in still water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> to complete the same length of swim, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is
questions.solution:
The total distance travelled by the man will be 2d. Therefore, the time taken by the man in still water will be,

t0=2d2v=dv

When the man is going downstream its speed will be equal to

v1=vm+vr=3v

Therefore, the time taken to go the distance d will be,

t1=dv1=d3v

When the man is going upstream its speed will be equal to

v2=vm-vr=v

Therefore, the time taken to go the distance d will be,

t2=dv2=dv

Therefore the total time taken is

t=t1+t2=4d3v⇒tt0=43

questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, heat given to a system is equal to the work done by the gas plus change in internal energy. Therefore,

Heat given in isobaric process will be,
